claim: Uncertainty distillation trains a model to convert its own Monte-Carlo sampling-based semantic uncertainty estimate into a verbalized confidence bin via supervised fine-tuning, requiring only a single forward pass at inference (no repeated sampling at test time).
stance_target: feasibility of distilling the internal sampling signal into verbal confidence, the target paper's core proposed angle
scope_conditions: QA tasks (MMLU, SocialIQA, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Ministral-8B, Gemini-2.5-flash-lite
quoted_support: We propose a simple procedure, uncertainty distillation, to teach an LLM to verbalize calibrated semantic confidences. Using held-out data to map initial uncertainty estimates to meaningful probabilities, we create examples annotated with verbalized probabilities for supervised fine-tuning.

claim: Uncertainty distillation achieves AUROC of 0.784 on Llama-3B/SocialIQA versus 0.601 for Semantic Entropy, despite Semantic Entropy requiring 20 samples and an entailment-model clustering step at inference time while uncertainty distillation uses a single generation.
stance_target: distillation of sampling signal into single-pass verbal confidence can match or exceed expensive multi-sample baselines
quoted_support: uncertainty distillation achieves AUROC of 0.784 with Llama-3B on SocialIQA, while semantic entropy achieves AUROC of 0.601.

claim: Uncertainty distillation's discrimination ceiling across QA benchmarks tops out around AUROC 0.69-0.79 (open-weight) and 0.762 (black-box Gemini), far below the near-perfect AUROC of internal sampling signals reported in code-LLM settings, indicating the verbal-bin encoding step itself loses substantial discriminative information relative to the raw sampling signal.
stance_target: whether existing distillation methods already close the calibration-disconnect gap fully
scope_conditions: MMLU, SocialIQA, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro; open-weight and black-box models
quoted_support: AUROC is consistently high with uncertainty distillation, generally outperforming other methods... AUROC is highest for uncertainty distillation for all experiments except Ministral-8B on SocialIQA

claim: Uncertainty distillation is never evaluated on code-generation tasks; all evaluation is on multiple-choice QA (MMLU, SocialIQA, MMLU-Pro) and open-answer math (GSM8K).
stance_target: domain gap between existing verbal-confidence distillation work and code LLMs
quoted_support: We demonstrate uncertainty distillation using two multiple-choice question answering datasets, the Massive Multitask Language Understanding benchmark (MMLU)... and the Social Interaction Question Answering dataset (SocialIQA).

claim: Uncertainty distillation representations of uncertainty transfer across domain shifts (e.g. trained on MMLU, tested on SocialIQA/OpenbookQA) and still outperform out-of-domain supervised baselines, suggesting the model learns a generalizable notion of its own reliability rather than memorizing per-topic error rates.
stance_target: generalizability of a sampling-signal-distilled verbal confidence model beyond its training distribution
quoted_support: we find that out-of-domain uncertainty distillation outperforms all unsupervised baselines (semantic entropy, prompting, and P(True)), with the sole exception of Ministral-8B semantic entropy on MMLU.

claim: Uncertainty distillation can be applied to black-box API models (Gemini-2.5-flash-lite) via API-based fine-tuning at a total pipeline cost of approximately $20, and outperforms 8x-32x more expensive semantic-entropy sampling at inference.
stance_target: practical feasibility/efficiency of distillation-based verbal confidence methods
quoted_support: The cost of running the entire pipeline was approximately $20, including generating samples, fine-tuning, and generating predictions on held-out data... we note that at inference uncertainty distillation only requires a single pass, while semantic entropy requires eight to thirty-two.

claim: Authors explicitly flag extension to multi-claim, long-form generation (beyond single-answer QA) and to tasks requiring LLM verifiers for correctness as open future work, and show an off-the-shelf pilot (CNN/DailyMail claim extraction) where verbalized confidence is poorly calibrated without their method.
stance_target: open problems in verbal confidence distillation that a code-LLM extension could address
quoted_support: By sampling multiple sets of claims for the same document, we can estimate the probability of each fact independently, and then apply our calibration and data augmentation procedure to fine-tune a model that outputs better calibrated confidences without incurring any additional runtime overhead.
